clause_text: Vendor's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed Rs. 500 regardless of the nature or severity of the claim.
why_risky: Liability cap of Rs. 500 is unreasonably low and contradicts ICA Section 73 which mandates reasonable compensation for breach.
safe_version: Vendor's total liability shall not exceed the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding 12 months.

clause_text: Client shall face no liability whatsoever for any damages caused to Vendor under any circumstances.
why_risky: Completely one-sided liability exclusion. Unenforceable under ICA Section 23 as it violates principles of fairness.
safe_version: Each party shall be liable for damages caused by their own negligence or willful misconduct.

clause_text: In no event shall either party be liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages.
why_risky: Broad exclusion of consequential damages may leave injured party with no meaningful remedy under ICA Section 73.
safe_version: Neither party shall be liable for indirect damages except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

clause_text: Client reserves the right to withhold payment indefinitely if it determines in its sole discretion that services were unsatisfactory.
why_risky: Unilateral indefinite payment withholding violates MSME Act Section 15 and ICA Section 73.
safe_version: Client may withhold disputed amounts only, with disputes resolved within 30 days through mutual negotiation.

clause_text: Client shall pay Vendor within 90 days of invoice receipt. No interest shall accrue on late payments.
why_risky: 90-day payment terms violate MSME Act Section 15 which mandates 45-day maximum. No interest clause further disadvantages vendor.
safe_version: Client shall pay Vendor within 45 days of invoice receipt. Late payments shall accrue compound interest at three times RBI bank rate per MSME Act Section 16.

clause_text: Client may set off any amounts owed by Vendor against payments due to Vendor without prior notice.
why_risky: Unilateral set-off without notice or dispute resolution process can be used to avoid legitimate payment obligations.
safe_version: Either party may set off amounts only after providing 30 days written notice and exhausting dispute resolution procedures.

clause_text: Client may terminate this Agreement at any time without notice and without cause. Upon termination Vendor forfeits all unpaid invoices.
why_risky: Immediate termination with invoice forfeiture is void under ICA Section 73. Vendor entitled to compensation for work done.
safe_version: Either party may terminate with 30 days written notice. Vendor shall be paid for all work completed prior to termination date.

clause_text: Vendor may not terminate this Agreement for any reason during the first 24 months.
why_risky: 24-month lock-in with no exit right for Vendor is heavily one-sided and above Indian market standard of 30-90 days.
safe_version: Either party may terminate for cause with 30 days notice. Vendor may terminate for convenience after 6 months with 60 days notice.

clause_text: Client may terminate immediately upon written notice if Vendor fails to meet any performance metric.
why_risky: Immediate termination for any performance failure without cure period is disproportionate and one-sided.
safe_version: Client may issue written notice of performance failure. Vendor shall have 30 days cure period before termination takes effect.

clause_text: Vendor shall keep all Client information strictly confidential for a period of lifetime.
why_risky: Lifetime confidentiality obligations are rarely enforceable in Indian courts and may constitute restraint of trade under ICA Section 27.
safe_version: Vendor shall maintain confidentiality for 5 years from disclosure date. Obligation survives termination for the same period.

clause_text: Confidential Information includes all information shared verbally or in writing with no requirement for marking.
why_risky: Overly broad definition with no marking requirement makes it impossible to know what is confidential, creating undue burden.
safe_version: Confidential Information means information marked as confidential at time of disclosure or confirmed in writing within 7 days of verbal disclosure.

clause_text: Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party without prior written consent.
why_risky: No carve-out for legally required disclosure to courts or regulators creates conflict with Indian legal obligations.
safe_version: Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information except where required by law, court order, or regulatory authority, with prior notice to Disclosing Party where permitted.

clause_text: All work product inventions code designs and deliverables created by Vendor shall become exclusive property of Client immediately upon creation. Vendor waives all moral rights permanently.
why_risky: Blanket IP assignment with moral rights waiver conflicts with Indian Copyright Act Section 57. Moral rights cannot be fully waived under Indian law.
safe_version: Client shall own all work product created specifically for this engagement. Vendor retains ownership of pre-existing IP and tools. Moral rights acknowledged per Copyright Act Section 57.

clause_text: Vendor grants Client an irrevocable perpetual royalty-free license to use all Vendor tools and software.
why_risky: Perpetual irrevocable license to all vendor tools without compensation or scope limitation is disproportionate.
safe_version: Vendor grants Client a non-exclusive license to use Vendor tools solely for purposes of this engagement during the contract term.

clause_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware USA. All disputes shall be resolved exclusively in courts located in Delaware USA.
why_risky: Foreign jurisdiction clause for Indian parties may violate ICA Section 28 which voids agreements restricting access to Indian courts.
safe_version: This Agreement shall be governed by Indian law. Disputes shall be resolved in courts of competent jurisdiction in Mumbai, India.

clause_text: Any disputes shall be resolved by arbitration in Singapore under ICC rules.
why_risky: Foreign arbitration seat adds significant cost burden for Indian parties and may conflict with Indian Arbitration Act provisions.
safe_version: Disputes shall be resolved by arbitration in Mumbai under Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996.

clause_text: Vendor shall indemnify Client from any and all claims damages losses and expenses including attorneys fees arising from Vendors performance whether or not caused by Clients negligence.
why_risky: Indemnity covering Client's own negligence is unenforceable under ICA Section 23 as it violates public policy principles.
safe_version: Vendor shall indemnify Client solely for claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Client indemnifies Vendor for Client's own negligence.

clause_text: Vendor shall indemnify Client for all third party intellectual property infringement claims without limitation.
why_risky: Unlimited IP indemnity without cap or carve-out for Client-provided specifications exposes Vendor to disproportionate risk.
safe_version: Vendor indemnifies Client for IP infringement arising from Vendor's work, capped at total contract value, excluding claims arising from Client specifications.

clause_text: Force majeure shall not apply to payment obligations. Client is not required to pay Vendor even if unable to receive services due to circumstances beyond Vendors control.
why_risky: Excluding payment from force majeure while keeping service delivery obligation one-sided contradicts ICA Section 56 on impossible contracts.
safe_version: Force majeure suspends obligations for both parties. Payment obligations are pro-rated for services rendered prior to force majeure event.

clause_text: Force majeure events include acts of God war and natural disasters but not pandemic epidemic or government action.
why_risky: Post-COVID Indian courts require explicit inclusion of pandemic and government action in force majeure definitions.
safe_version: Force majeure includes acts of God, war, natural disasters, pandemic, epidemic, and government actions that make performance impossible or illegal.

clause_text: Vendor shall not work with any company in any industry anywhere in the world for a period of 5 years after termination.
why_risky: Global non-compete for 5 years is void under ICA Section 27 which prohibits agreements in restraint of trade.
safe_version: Vendor shall not solicit Client's existing customers in the same geographic region for 1 year post termination.

clause_text: Client may modify the scope of services at any time without notice and without adjustment to fees or timeline.
why_risky: Unilateral scope modification without fee adjustment creates unlimited obligation for Vendor without compensation.
safe_version: Scope modifications require mutual written agreement with corresponding adjustments to fees and timeline.

clause_text: This Agreement may be assigned by Client to any third party without Vendor consent.
why_risky: Unilateral assignment without consent could transfer Vendor obligations to an unknown third party.
safe_version: Neither party may assign this Agreement without prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld.
